description: A machine costs \$24000, has a salvage value of \$4000, and a useful life of 5 years. Using straight-line depreciation what is the annual depreciation expense?
explanation: Straight-line depreciation = (Cost - Salvage Value) / Useful Life = (\$24000 - \$4000) / 5 = \$20000 / 5 = \$4000 per year.
hint: (Cost - Salvage) / Life

description: A company has net income of \$45000, interest expense of \$5000, and income tax expense of \$15000. What is EBIT?
explanation: EBIT = Net Income + Interest Expense + Income Tax Expense = \$45000 + \$5000 + \$15000 = \$65000. EBIT measures operating profitability before financing and tax costs.
hint: EBIT = Net Income + Interest + Taxes

description: On March 1 a company receives \$18000 cash for a 6-month service contract. What is the journal entry on March 1?
explanation: Receiving cash before performing the service creates a liability (unearned revenue). Debit Cash \$18000 and credit Unearned Revenue \$18000. Revenue will be recognized as services are performed.
choice0: Debit Cash \$18000 and Credit Unearned Revenue \$18000
choice1: Debit Cash \$18000 and Credit Service Revenue \$18000
choice2: Debit Unearned Revenue \$18000 and Credit Cash \$18000
choice3: Debit Accounts Receivable \$18000 and Credit Service Revenue \$18000

description: Using the double-declining-balance method a \$10000 asset with a 5-year life has what depreciation expense in Year 1?
explanation: DDB rate = 2 / Useful Life = 2 / 5 = 40%. Year 1 depreciation = Book Value x DDB Rate = \$10000 x 40% = \$4000.
hint: DDB Rate = 2 / Life; Depreciation = Book Value x Rate

description: Current assets = \$90000, current liabilities = \$30000, inventory = \$20000, prepaid expenses = \$5000. What is the quick ratio?
explanation: Quick Ratio = (Current Assets - Inventory - Prepaid Expenses) / Current Liabilities = (\$90000 - \$20000 - \$5000) / \$30000 = \$65000 / \$30000 = 2.17.
hint: Quick Ratio = (CA - Inventory - Prepaid) / CL

description: A company starts with 100 units at \$10 each. During the period it buys 200 units at \$12 each. It sells 150 units. Using FIFO what is the cost of goods sold?
explanation: FIFO sells the oldest inventory first. First 100 units at \$10 = \$1000. Next 50 units at \$12 = \$600. Total COGS = \$1600. The remaining 150 units in ending inventory cost \$12 each = \$1800.
hint: FIFO: sell oldest first

description: A company pays \$5000 per week (Mon-Fri). The last payroll was paid December 26 (Friday). December 31 is a Wednesday. What salary accrual is needed?
explanation: Employees worked 3 days (Mon Dec 29, Tue Dec 30, Wed Dec 31). Daily wage = \$5000 / 5 = \$1000/day. Accrual = 3 x \$1000 = \$3000. Debit Salaries Expense \$3000, Credit Salaries Payable \$3000.
hint: Daily wage = weekly / 5; Multiply by days worked

description: Sales = \$500000, COGS = \$300000, Operating Expenses = \$100000, Interest Expense = \$20000, Tax Rate = 25%. What is net income?
An asset costs \$50000, has a salvage value of \$5000, and a useful life of 9 years. Using sum-of-years-digits (SYD) what is depreciation in Year 1?
explanation: SYD = n(n+1)/2 = 9(10)/2 = 45. Depreciable base = \$50000 - \$5000 = \$45000. Year 1 fraction = 9 / 45. Year 1 depreciation = \$45000 x (9 / 45) = \$9000.
hint: SYD = n(n+1)/2; Year 1 dep = Base x (n/SYD)

description: Beginning inventory = 50 units at \$20. Purchases: 100 units at \$25. Sales = 80 units. Using weighted average cost what is COGS?
explanation: Weighted average cost = Total Cost / Total Units = (50 x \$20 + 100 x \$25) / 150 = \$3500 / 150 = \$23.33 per unit. COGS = 80 x \$23.33 = \$1867 (rounded).
hint: Avg Cost = Total Cost / Total Units; COGS = Units Sold x Avg Cost

description: A company buys equipment worth \$40000 by paying \$10000 cash and financing the rest with a 3-year note. What journal entry records this?
explanation: Buying an asset with partial cash and partial note: debit Equipment \$40000 (full cost), credit Cash \$10000, credit Notes Payable \$30000 (liability for the financed portion).
choice0: Debit Equipment \$40000 - Credit Cash \$10000 - Credit Notes Payable \$30000
choice2: Debit Cash \$10000 and Debit Notes Payable \$30000 and Credit Equipment \$40000
choice3: Debit Equipment \$40000 and Credit Notes Payable \$40000

description: A company has net income of \$80000 and average stockholders equity of \$400000. What is the return on equity (ROE)?
explanation: Return on Equity = Net Income / Average Stockholders Equity = \$80000 / \$400000 = 0.20 or 20%.
hint: ROE = Net Income / Average Equity

description: A company prepays \$24000 for a 24-month office lease on July 1 Year 1. On December 31 Year 1 what is the adjusting entry?
explanation: By December 31, 6 months of the 24-month lease have expired. Monthly expense = \$24000 / 24 = \$1000. Expense for 6 months = \$6000. Debit Rent Expense \$6000 and Credit Prepaid Rent \$6000.
hint: Monthly exp = Total / Months; Expense = Monthly x Months Used
choice0: Debit Prepaid Rent \$1000 and Credit Cash \$1000
choice1: Debit Rent Expense \$6000 and Credit Prepaid Rent \$6000
choice2: Debit Rent Expense \$24000 and Credit Prepaid Rent \$24000
choice3: Debit Rent Expense \$12000 and Credit Prepaid Rent \$12000

description: Total assets = \$500000. Debt-to-equity ratio = 1.5. What is total equity?
explanation: Debt-to-equity = Liabilities / Equity = 1.5 so Liabilities = 1.5E. Assets = Liabilities + Equity gives \$500000 = 1.5E + E = 2.5E. Equity = \$500000 / 2.5 = \$200000.
hint: Assets = Liabilities + Equity; D/E = Liabilities / Equity

description: An asset with book value of \$8000 (cost \$20000, accumulated depreciation \$12000) is sold for \$10000. What is the gain or loss?
explanation: Gain/Loss = Sale Price - Book Value = \$10000 - \$8000 = \$2000 gain. Since the sale price exceeds book value there is a gain.
hint: Book Value = Cost - Accum. Dep.; Gain/Loss = Sale Price - Book Value
choice0: \$2000 gain
choice3: \$8000 gain

description: A company has sales of \$600000 and average inventory of \$100000. What is inventory turnover and the average days to sell inventory?
explanation: Inventory Turnover = Sales / Avg Inventory = 600000 / 100000 = 6 times. Days in inventory = 365 / 6 = 60.8 days (approximately 61 days).
hint: Inv. Turnover = Sales / Avg Inv; Days = 365 / Turnover
choice0: 6 times - 73 days
choice2: 12 times - 30 days
choice3: 6 times - 61 days

description: A company estimates 2% of credit sales of \$200000 will be uncollectible. Record the bad debt entry using the income statement approach.
explanation: Bad Debt Expense = 2% x \$200000 = \$4000. Debit Bad Debt Expense \$4000 and Credit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts \$4000.
choice0: Debit Accounts Receivable \$4000 and Credit Bad Debt Expense \$4000
choice1: Debit Bad Debt Expense \$4000 and Credit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts \$4000
choice2: Debit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts \$4000 and Credit Bad Debt Expense \$4000
choice3: Debit Cash \$4000 and Credit Accounts Receivable \$4000

description: Net income = \$70000. Depreciation = \$15000. Accounts receivable increased \$8000. Inventory decreased \$5000. Accounts payable increased \$3000. What is operating cash flow (indirect method)?
explanation: OCF = Net Income + Depreciation - Increase in AR + Decrease in Inv + Increase in AP = \$70000 + \$15000 - \$8000 + \$5000 + \$3000 = \$85000.
hint: OCF = NI + Depreciation +/- Changes in Working Capital

description: A company reports EPS = \$4.00 and the stock price is \$60. What is the price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio?
explanation: P/E Ratio = Market Price per Share / Earnings per Share = \$60 / \$4 = 15. A P/E of 15 means investors pay \$15 for every \$1 of earnings.
hint: P/E = Market Price / EPS

description: On November 1 a company lends \$30000 at 6% annual interest. The fiscal year ends December 31. What interest revenue should be accrued?
explanation: Interest accrued = \$30000 x 6% x (2 / 12) = \$300. Two months (November and December) of interest must be accrued even though cash is not yet received.
hint: Interest = Principal x Rate x (Months / 12)

description: A company using LIFO has a LIFO reserve of \$40000. Pretax income under LIFO is \$100000. What would pretax income be under FIFO?
explanation: FIFO pretax income = LIFO pretax income + LIFO reserve = \$100000 + \$40000 = \$140000. FIFO results in higher income when prices are rising.
hint: FIFO Income = LIFO Income + LIFO Reserve

description: A company issues 1000 shares of \$1 par value common stock at \$15 per share. Record the journal entry.
explanation: Total cash = 1000 x \$15 = \$15000. Common Stock (par) = 1000 x \$1 = \$1000. APIC = \$15000 - \$1000 = \$14000. Debit Cash \$15000, Credit Common Stock \$1000, Credit APIC \$14000.
choice0: Debit Cash \$15000 and Credit Common Stock \$15000
choice1: Debit Common Stock \$1000 and Credit Cash \$15000
choice2: Debit Cash \$15000 - Credit Common Stock \$1000 - Credit Additional Paid-in Capital \$14000
choice3: Debit Cash \$1000 and Credit Common Stock \$1000

description: A company has total assets of \$300000, long-term liabilities of \$80000, and current liabilities of \$50000. What is stockholders equity?
explanation: Stockholders Equity = Total Assets - Total Liabilities = \$300000 - (\$80000 + \$50000) = \$300000 - \$130000 = \$170000.
hint: Equity = Assets - Liabilities

description: A company buys a vehicle for \$30000, expects to drive it 150000 miles, and estimates salvage value of \$3000. In Year 1 the vehicle is driven 30000 miles. What is depreciation under units-of-production?
hint: Dep rate = (Cost - Salvage) / Total units; Dep = Rate x Units used

description: Net income = \$120000, total assets = \$800000. What is the return on assets (ROA)?
explanation: ROA = Net Income / Total Assets = \$120000 / \$800000 = 0.15 or 15%. ROA measures how efficiently the company uses its assets to generate profit.
hint: ROA = Net Income / Total Assets

description: Which of the following would be classified as an investing activity on the statement of cash flows?
explanation: Purchasing land is an investing activity because it involves acquiring a long-term asset. Paying dividends is financing. Paying salaries and collecting from customers are operating activities.
choice0: Paying dividends to shareholders
choice2: Purchasing land for \$200000
choice3: Paying salaries to employees

description: A company accrues wages of \$8000 at December 31 and pays them on January 5. Show the January 5 entry.
explanation: At December 31 the accrual was: debit Wages Expense and credit Wages Payable for \$8000. On January 5 the liability is eliminated: debit Wages Payable \$8000 and credit Cash \$8000.
choice0: Debit Wages Payable \$8000 and Credit Cash \$8000
choice1: Debit Wages Expense \$8000 and Credit Cash \$8000
choice2: Debit Cash \$8000 and Credit Wages Payable \$8000
choice3: Debit Wages Expense \$8000 and Credit Wages Payable \$8000

description: A company has net income of \$200000, preferred dividends of \$20000, and 90000 weighted average common shares outstanding. What is EPS?
explanation: EPS = (Net Income - Preferred Dividends) / Weighted Average Common Shares = (\$200000 - \$20000) / 90000 = \$180000 / 90000 = \$2.00 per share.
hint: EPS = (Net Income - Preferred Dividends) / WACSO

description: On September 1 a company receives \$36000 for a 12-month service contract. By December 31 how much revenue has been earned and what remains in unearned revenue?
explanation: By December 31, 4 months have been completed (Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec). Monthly = \$36000 / 12 = \$3000. Earned = 4 x \$3000 = \$12000. Unearned = \$36000 - \$12000 = \$24000.
hint: Monthly revenue = Total / 12; Earned = Months completed x Monthly
choice0: Earned \$6000 - Unearned \$30000
choice2: Earned \$36000 - Unearned \$0
choice3: Earned \$9000 - Unearned \$27000

description: At the start of the year retained earnings = \$50000. During the year: net income = \$30000 and dividends declared = \$10000. What is ending retained earnings?
explanation: Ending Retained Earnings = Beginning RE + Net Income - Dividends = \$50000 + \$30000 - \$10000 = \$70000.
hint: Ending RE = Beginning RE + Net Income - Dividends

description: Equipment cost \$15000 with no salvage value and a 5-year straight-line life. What is book value at the END of Year 2?
explanation: Annual depreciation = \$15000 / 5 = \$3000. Accumulated depreciation after Year 2 = \$3000 x 2 = \$6000. Book Value = \$15000 - \$6000 = \$9000.
hint: Annual dep = Cost / Life; Book Value = Cost - Accum Dep

description: A bond with a face value of \$100000 is issued at 98 (98% of face value). Record the journal entry.
explanation: Cash received = \$100000 x 98% = \$98000. The \$2000 difference is a discount (contra-liability). Debit Cash \$98000, Debit Discount on Bonds Payable \$2000, Credit Bonds Payable \$100000.
choice0: Debit Cash \$100000 and Credit Bonds Payable \$100000
choice1: Debit Cash \$98000 and Credit Bonds Payable \$98000
choice2: Debit Bonds Payable \$100000 - Credit Cash \$98000 - Credit Bond Premium \$2000
choice3: Debit Cash \$98000 - Debit Discount on Bonds Payable \$2000 - Credit Bonds Payable \$100000

description: Beginning accounts receivable = \$40000. Ending accounts receivable = \$60000. Net credit sales = \$500000. What is the average collection period (days)?
explanation: Average AR = (\$40000 + \$60000) / 2 = \$50000. AR Turnover = \$500000 / \$50000 = 10. Average Collection Period = 365 / 10 = 36.5 days.
hint: Avg AR = (Beg + End) / 2; Turnover = Sales / Avg AR; Days = 365 / Turnover
choice0: 30 days
choice2: 50 days
choice3: 25 days

description: A company sells 500 units at \$20 each. Variable cost per unit = \$12. Fixed costs = \$3000. What is operating income?
explanation: Contribution margin per unit = \$20 - \$12 = \$8. Total CM = \$8 x 500 = \$4000. Operating Income = \$4000 - \$3000 = \$1000.
hint: CM = (Price - Variable Cost) x Units; OI = CM - Fixed Costs

description: Net income = \$50000. Gain on sale of equipment = \$8000. Depreciation = \$12000. Increase in accounts receivable = \$5000. What is operating cash flow using indirect method?
explanation: OCF = Net Income + Depreciation - Gain on Sale - Increase in AR = \$50000 + \$12000 - \$8000 - \$5000 = \$49000. Gains are subtracted; increases in AR reduce operating cash.
hint: OCF = NI + Dep - Gains + Losses +/- WC changes

description: COGS formula for a merchandiser: Beginning Inventory = \$10000, Purchases = \$60000, Ending Inventory = \$15000. What is COGS?
explanation: COGS = Beginning Inventory + Purchases - Ending Inventory = \$10000 + \$60000 - \$15000 = \$55000.
hint: COGS = Beg. Inv + Purchases - End. Inv

description: When a company changes its inventory costing method from FIFO to weighted average what must it do?
explanation: A change in accounting principle requires retrospective application - restating all prior periods as if the new method had always been used.
choice0: Record the change as a current period expense
choice1: Apply the change retrospectively and restate prior period financial statements
choice2: Disclose the change but make no adjustments
choice3: Apply the change only to future inventory purchases

description: A company discovers an error: \$5000 of supplies expense was recorded as equipment. Supplies have been fully used. Record the correcting entry.
explanation: The original entry incorrectly debited Equipment. To correct: debit Supplies Expense \$5000 and credit Equipment \$5000 (removes the wrong asset and records the right expense).
choice0: Debit Equipment \$5000 and Credit Supplies Expense \$5000
choice2: Debit Supplies Expense \$5000 and Credit Equipment \$5000
choice3: Debit Cash \$5000 and Credit Equipment \$5000

description: Quick assets (cash + AR) = \$120000 and current liabilities = \$80000. What is the quick ratio and what does it indicate?
explanation: Quick Ratio = Quick Assets / Current Liabilities = \$120000 / \$80000 = 1.5. A ratio above 1.0 means the company can cover current liabilities with its most liquid assets.
hint: Quick Ratio = Quick Assets / Current Liabilities
choice0: 1.5 - company can cover current liabilities without selling inventory
choice2: 2.0 - company is highly liquid
choice3: 1.5 - company should borrow more

description: Equipment cost \$36000 with no salvage value and a 6-year life. Using double-declining balance what is book value at the end of Year 2?
hint: DDB Rate = 2 / Life; Apply rate to book value each year

description: Common Stock = \$50000, APIC = \$30000, Retained Earnings = \$40000, Treasury Stock = (\$10000). What is total stockholders equity?
explanation: Total Stockholders Equity = Common Stock + APIC + Retained Earnings - Treasury Stock = \$50000 + \$30000 + \$40000 - \$10000 = \$110000.

description: A company signs a note payable for \$20000 on October 1 at 9% annual interest. The fiscal year ends December 31. What interest accrual is needed?
explanation: Interest = \$20000 x 9% x (3 / 12) = \$450. Three months (October, November, December) must be accrued. Debit Interest Expense \$450, Credit Interest Payable \$450.
hint: Interest = Principal x Rate x (Months/12)

description: Given: Sales \$400000, Sales Returns \$10000, COGS \$200000, Selling expenses \$50000, Admin expenses \$30000, Interest expense \$8000, Tax rate 20%. What is net income?
explanation: Net Sales = \$390000. Gross Profit = \$190000. Operating Income = \$110000. EBT = \$102000. Tax = \$102000 x 20% = \$20400. Net Income = \$81600.

description: A company sells equipment with book value of \$15000 for \$19000 cash. How is this reported on the cash flow statement?
explanation: The \$19000 proceeds are reported in investing activities. Under the indirect method the \$4000 gain is subtracted from net income in the operating section because it is already captured in investing.
choice0: \$15000 inflow in operating activities
choice2: \$19000 inflow in operating with gain added
choice3: \$19000 inflow in investing activities with \$4000 gain removed from operating

description: On April 1 \$6000 cash is received for a 1-year service contract. On December 31 (9 months later) what is the adjusting entry?
explanation: Nine months of the 12-month contract are completed. Earned revenue = 9 / 12 x \$6000 = \$4500. Debit Unearned Revenue \$4500 and Credit Service Revenue \$4500.
hint: Earned = (Months completed / Total months) x Total
choice0: Debit Unearned Revenue \$6000 and Credit Service Revenue \$6000
choice1: Debit Unearned Revenue \$4500 and Credit Service Revenue \$4500
choice2: Debit Service Revenue \$4500 and Credit Unearned Revenue \$4500
choice3: Debit Unearned Revenue \$1500 and Credit Service Revenue \$1500

description: Total assets = \$1000000. Total liabilities = \$600000. Net income = \$80000. What is the debt ratio and ROA?
hint: Debt Ratio = Liabilities / Assets; ROA = Net Income / Assets
choice0: Debt Ratio 40% and ROA 12%
choice2: Debt Ratio 60% and ROA 8%
choice3: Debt Ratio 60% and ROA 13%

description: A company purchases a patent for \$90000 with a legal life of 20 years and estimated useful life of 15 years. What is the annual amortization using straight-line?
explanation: Intangible assets are amortized over the shorter of legal life or useful economic life. The shorter is 15 years. Annual amortization = \$90000 / 15 = \$6000 per year.
hint: Amortize over the shorter of legal or useful life; Annual = Cost / Life

description: FIFO inventory records: Jan 1 = 200 units at \$5. Jan 15 purchase = 300 units at \$6. Jan 20 sale = 400 units. What is ending inventory value?
explanation: FIFO: 400 units sold - first 200 at \$5 = \$1000, next 200 at \$6 = \$1200, COGS = \$2200. Remaining: 100 units at \$6 = \$600 ending inventory.
hint: FIFO: sell oldest units first; remaining inventory at newest cost

description: Beginning RE = \$100000. Net loss = \$15000. Cash dividends declared = \$5000. Stock dividends declared = \$8000. What is ending retained earnings?
explanation: Ending RE = \$100000 - \$15000 - \$5000 - \$8000 = \$72000. Both cash and stock dividends reduce retained earnings.
hint: Ending RE = Beginning RE +/- Net Income(Loss) - Dividends

description: Under IFRS which presentation method for operating cash flows is generally preferred?
explanation: IFRS encourages (but does not require) the direct method for presenting operating cash flows - showing actual cash inflows and outflows.
choice0: Indirect method
choice2: Direct method
choice3: Hybrid method
